jtbd: Decide whether and how to widen the arcs-algorethics Decision Firewall beyond its current narrow tripwire. Ground truth (2026-09-15, PR #8): on AgentHarm test_public (176 harmful + 176 benign agentic tasks with real tool-call names) the gate locks 0/176 harmful and 0/176 benign, with or without the task prompt in the payload. Structural causes: (1) harmful and benign tasks call the SAME functions (send_email, post_on_x, get_webpage); harm lives in arguments and intent, invisible to name-matching; (2) invariants cover lethal force, vital care, livelihood only; AgentHarm's eight categories (fraud, harassment, cybercrime, drugs, hate, sexual, copyright, disinformation) are none of those. Free-text sets (hendrycks/ethics deontology, JailBreakV-28k) are 0% too, by design. Everything around the gate is real and green: daemon with Ed25519-signed resume + operator key custody, ledger migration (Docker-verified, gate_receipts), ops CLI, nightly benchmarks committed to benchmarks/history/, arcs-v9 Edge route (PR #446, keyed, unmerged). Two honest options: (A) argument-aware rules per tool (a policy table keyed by tool name + argument predicates, e.g. send_email to >N recipients, post_* with generated media, any *pay*/*transfer* over a threshold), deterministic, auditable, still narrow; (B) a classifier in the loop (Llama-Guard / small DeBERTa / a Claude call) over (tool, args, prompt), broad, non-deterministic, needs its own eval + latency budget vs the 4.5ms SLA. Or (C) leave it a narrow tripwire and say so (README already does). Decision, not patch.
